weights.note: BASE weights of the technique; decisio itself ships no weights

licence.notes: decisio code is Apache-2.0 (README badge, LICENSE, NOTICE). The Gemma 4 31B base is published by Google as Apache-2.0 on its HF card; the card links the Gemma 4 licence page. Installer downloads the base from HF; nothing is rehosted.

jev_distillation.evidence: "Official checkpoint from Google, at a pinned revision; no adapter or fine-tuning by us" (decisio README, base table). Decisio is a serving layer over the frozen base; no training described.

installer_policy.reason: Serves an unmodified Google base with a wire-format layer; no training data and no Jev outputs described. Commercial use follows the base licence.

readout.notes: Decisio vllm_engine (decisio.serve.vllm_engine, --base gemma-4-31b) on vLLM 0.30.0 with FP8 quantisation on load; one prefill per state, probabilities from option tokens. vLLM-specific engine, not an OpenAI logprobs call.
readout.portable_notes: No portable variant for this 31B configuration. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aminry/decisio/5b42101a191d222062a795194b0aedb5003bf6ea/src/decisio/serve/vllm_engine.py L959: if args.backend == "mlx" and args.base == "gemma-4-31b":; L960: raise ValueError("--backend mlx serves the Qwen base and gemma-4-12b; gemma-4-31b is served on vLLM only"). The author has an FP32 CPU smoke-test stand-in (hf_letters.py L3–10, L39), explicitly not for measurement; it would require ~125.1 GB weights and ~156.4 GB with 25% headroom. 31B CPU execution is not practical. The 62.546 GB BF16 base +25% exceeds a 64 GB Mac; a 96/128 GB Mac has more memory, but the author rejects this base on MLX. Other supported MLX bases are different models and are not substituted. Frozen base uses FP8-on-load in the BH recipe, not a trained checkpoint.

steps: git clone github.com/aminry/decisio @ 5b42101a; uv sync --extra serve --frozen (lockfile in repo).
Download google/gemma-4-31B-it @ 842da379 (two safetensors shards, index, configs).
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1; cd decisio; uv run --frozen python -m decisio.serve.vllm_engine --base gemma-4-31b --port 8000.

measured.gpu: UNVERIFIED: the BH card for this row is not recorded in the files read (author README mentions a 96 GB card)

variants.expected_speed: About 47 ms p 50 per decision (raw, serial) on the BH card; the author reports 56 ms median on its own run. Provisioning class: RTX PRO 6000 96 GB; this names a memory class, not a latency measurement or confirmation of architecture compatibility. CPU/Mac speed is estimated only in separate portable variants.
variants.notes: min_vram_gb left null: the decisio README gives 30.6 GiB in memory for gemma-4-31b after FP8 load, plus KV, but no minimum card; recommended 96 is the author card. Benchmarked base revision 842da379 is the one the decisio README pins. Base weights 62.55 GB bf16 on disk. Host RAM provisioning estimate: pinned weight files sum to 62.546 GB; ×1.25 loader/runtime allowance rounded up to 4 GB gives 80 GB. This is not a measured peak; FP32 initialization or duplicate weight buffers may require more. VRAM estimate, not measured minimum: 62.546 GB BF16 files /2 for FP8-on-load ≈31.273 GB (+scales/unquantized layers). Pinned config has 10 full-attention layers, 4 global KV heads at dimension512 and 50 sliding layers, 16 KV heads at dimension256, window1024. At max_model_len32768, an unshared BF16 single-sequence K/V upper estimate is 3.523 GB; weights+KV plus ~25% weight allowance ≈42.6 GB, / gpu_memory_utilization0.90 ≈47.4 GB. Round to 48 GB for a single serial request; warmed prefixes/concurrency/multimodal inputs can exceed this. Recommend96 GB (author RTX PRO6000 class; BH GPU not verified), not a guarantee the unchanged default recipe fits 48 GB. Executable recipe provenance and runtime differences: catalog/TEXT-RECIPES-V2.md. Recipe verified.status is unverified; package resolution and command expansion do not establish inference parity.
